title: Union trouble as a transfer member from Milwaukee
summary: The Chicago local blocked him from a Regal Theater job as a transfer member, but could not remove him from Louis Armstrong's band because Armstrong insisted.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: When you first came to Chicago -- I've done some reading about this -- and it seems like there were three kinds of jobs. There was theater jobs, ballroom jobs, and then cabaret jobs, where the small bands played. And there seemed to be some resistence among the theater and ballroom leaders, such as Doc Cook, Charlie Elgar, Dave Peyton, to the cabaret musicians -- a lot of the New Orleans musicians didn't were there because, I guess, because they couldn't read so well. Did you sense any of this?

No, because I guess I was busy trying to weather the storm of my own thing by being transfer member from Milwaukee in here, and it looked like this union had it in for transfer members, because I was to go into Regal Theater with Jerome Carrington and I think George Smith was president
and he didn't let me go.
Yeah, the local 208 -- those men I mentioned were quite influential in union affairs also.

Yeah, he didn't let me go in there and when I got with Louie, he came out -- came down there to pull me off, I think, either he or Art Stewart, one of the two -- I don't know which one, came down there to pull me off the job there, but --
Yeah, but they couldn't do nothing there because Louie was the one hired me and he wanted me and they put their foot out there -- put their foot down so they had to go along with the program.
